summary: All 6 R5 findings (R5-NEW-MAJ-001, R5-NEW-MAJ-002 ×3 lenses, R5-NEW-MIN-001, R5-NEW-nit-001) are genuinely closed. The fix-round-5 companion sweep closures (§5.6 branch-protection-log clarification + §8 blocked-on-adopter-conflict non-counting) are confirmed landed. However, the R5 safety MAJ-002 fix — which added the meaningful-content regex spec to invariant 2 — introduced two new MAJ that prevent fixpoint: (1) the regex scope header says 'STATUS.md list marker' but the blocked-on-adopter-conflict CI check targets DISPATCH-NOTE, creating an unspecified file/format requirement for the conflict-path TF reference; (2) the regex terminal clause '.{20,}' (any 20 characters including whitespace) contradicts the prose description '≥20 non-whitespace characters of description', leaving two different implementations possible for a Codex executor told to 'implement this regex literally'. A new MIN is also present: §5.6 first Threshold A bullet conflates the ≥3 counting criterion with the invocation-log-entries-committed requirement in a way that is inconsistent with §8's first bullet, which separates them. Fixpoint not reached.

regex_format_spec_scan.finding: The format spec block added by R5 (invariant 2 lines 49–58) introduces two internal inconsistencies that defeat the machine-enforceability goal and create implementation ambiguity for the Codex executor implementing check-invocation-log-entry.sh. See R6-NEW-MAJ-001 (STATUS.md scope vs DISPATCH-NOTE check) and R6-NEW-MAJ-002 (.{20,} vs '≥20 non-whitespace').

conflicts.description: The scope header says 'STATUS.md list marker', implying the regex applies to STATUS.md scanning only. But the blocked-on-adopter-conflict CI check (invariant 2 line 47, R-024-06 line 219) explicitly targets DISPATCH-NOTE. The regex requires '^- **TF-' prefix (a STATUS.md bullet format); DISPATCH-NOTE content may use a different format. The spec does not say the DISPATCH-NOTE TF reference must use STATUS.md bullet format, nor does it clarify what file check-invocation-log-entry.sh scans for the conflict path.

The regex uses '.{20,}' which matches any 20 characters including whitespace (spaces, tabs). The prose description says '≥20 non-whitespace characters of description'. These are different specifications: a description of 20 spaces satisfies .{20,} but has zero non-whitespace characters. The spec says 'check-invocation-log-entry.sh (024B) implements this regex literally', so an executor following the literal regex gets different behavior from one following the prose description. The machine-enforceability goal of R5-NEW-MAJ-002 safety is only partially met: the spec added a regex to resolve ambiguity but the regex and its prose description disagree on what they enforce.

In practice these are operationally equivalent (onboarded/onboarded-operator-bump paths cannot have check-live without a log entry), but the formal criteria are different and a reviewer cross-checking §5.6 against §8 would find a discrepancy.

findings.title: Invariant 2 meaningful-content format spec scoped to 'STATUS.md list marker' but blocked-on-adopter-conflict CI check targets DISPATCH-NOTE — the regex's file/format applicability to DISPATCH-NOTE TF references is unspecified, creating implementation ambiguity for check-invocation-log-entry.sh
findings.evidence: Invariant 2 format spec header (line 49): 'TF-024X rows MUST match the regex (anchored, after a leading `- ` STATUS.md list marker)'. The parenthetical scope qualifier 'STATUS.md list marker' tells a Codex executor implementing check-invocation-log-entry.sh that the regex applies to STATUS.md list items (markdown bullets starting with '- '). However: (1) invariant 2 line 47 says blocked-on-adopter-conflict PR 'MUST reference the filed TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> TF in DISPATCH-NOTE... (format spec below)' — the TF reference is in DISPATCH-NOTE, not STATUS.md; (2) R-024-06 line 219 says 'check-invocation-log-entry.sh (a) verifies the TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> reference IS present in DISPATCH-NOTE with meaningful content matching invariant 2's regex spec' — confirming the check scans DISPATCH-NOTE; (3) the regex requires the matching line to begin with '^- **TF-...' (a STATUS.md-style bullet prefix). A Codex executor implementing the check faces three ambiguous paths: (a) scan STATUS.md for a TF-024X-conflict row (but the spec says 'referenced in DISPATCH-NOTE', not 'STATUS.md row'); (b) scan DISPATCH-NOTE for a line matching the regex (requires DISPATCH-NOTE to contain a STATUS.md-formatted bullet — not specified); (c) scan DISPATCH-NOTE for any reference to the TF prefix regardless of format (but the regex is literal and includes the '- **' prefix). Contrast with onboarded-operator-bump (R-024-07): R-024-07 line 220 explicitly says 'STATUS.md Tracked-forward items row using exactly the standardised prefix' and 'the CI script verifies STATUS.md contains the matching TF row'. The blocked-on-adopter-conflict path has no analogous explicit file + format specification. The gap is MAJ because check-invocation-log-entry.sh's implementation for the blocked-on-adopter-conflict path is not deterministic from the current spec: two Codex executors could produce different implementations that pass some cases and fail others.
findings.recommendation: Fix the format spec header and/or the blocked-on-adopter-conflict specification to resolve the file/format ambiguity. Option A (simpler): Change invariant 2 line 47 to say 'MUST include a STATUS.md Tracked-forward items row for TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> (matching the format spec below) AND MUST reference that TF in DISPATCH-NOTE (prose or structured)'; update §5.2 line 130, §6 024B line 201, and R-024-06 line 219 to use the same 'STATUS.md Tracked-forward items row' phrasing. Option B: Change the format spec header from 'STATUS.md list marker' to 'STATUS.md or DISPATCH-NOTE TF row' and add a sentence clarifying that for blocked-on-adopter-conflict, the check-invocation-log-entry.sh script scans DISPATCH-NOTE for a line matching the regex. Either option must be propagated to all four specification sites (invariant 2, §5.2, §6 024B, R-024-06).

findings.title: Invariant 2 meaningful-content format spec: regex terminal clause '.{20,}' (any 20 characters including whitespace) contradicts prose description '≥20 non-whitespace characters of description' — spec is internally inconsistent, partially re-opening the machine-enforceability gap that R5-NEW-MAJ-002 safety aimed to close
findings.evidence: Invariant 2 format spec block (lines 49–58). The regex (line 52): '^- \*\*TF-024X-(renovate|conflict)-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+\*\* \((open|pending|in-progress|closed)\): .{20,}$'. The terminal clause '.{20,}' uses the regex dot character '.' which by default matches any character (including space, tab, etc.) — any 20 characters total. The prose description immediately following the regex (line 55): '...then ≥20 non-whitespace characters of description.' The prose uses 'non-whitespace characters', which corresponds to the regex character class '\S' (not '.'), i.e. \S{20,}. These are different acceptance predicates: a description of 20 whitespace characters satisfies '.{20,}' but has zero non-whitespace characters; a description of 'a                   ' (letter + 19 spaces = 20 chars) satisfies '.{20,}' but has only 1 non-whitespace character. The spec then says (line 55): 'check-invocation-log-entry.sh (024B) implements this regex literally.' An executor following the regex literally implements .{20,} = any-20-chars. An executor following the prose implements \S{20,} = 20-non-whitespace-chars. The R5-NEW-MAJ-002 safety fix was motivated by the goal of a 'precise regex spec' that is 'machine-enforceable' so 'Codex executors implementing check-invocation-log-entry.sh use this regex literally.' The fix achieves a regex spec, but the regex and its description disagree on the description-length predicate, which is the core of the meaningful-content requirement. A description padded with spaces (e.g. '(open):                      x') would pass the regex but fail the prose. This defeats the machine-enforceability goal for the description-length dimension. The examples given all have clearly substantive descriptions (>20 non-whitespace chars), so the examples don't expose this inconsistency. But the spec itself is internally inconsistent on the precise predicate it intends to enforce.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the inconsistency by aligning the regex with the prose. Since the intent is clearly to require substantive description content (the examples and context all support 'non-whitespace'), the correct fix is to change the regex terminal clause from '.{20,}' to '\S{20,}' (20 or more non-whitespace characters). Update line 52 regex: '^- \*\*TF-024X-(renovate|conflict)-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+\*\* \((open|pending|in-progress|closed)\): \S.{19,}$' or equivalently '...\): \S.*\S.{18,}$' — but the simplest correct expression matching '≥20 non-whitespace characters after the colon+space' is to use a non-whitespace-anchored spec. Alternatively, if the intent is 'any 20 characters' (i.e. the prose is wrong and the regex is right), update the prose on line 55 to read '≥20 characters of description (any character including spaces)'. The prose-to-regex path (change regex to \S{20,}) is strongly preferred given the security intent: it closes the whitespace-padding bypass. Add a closes marker for this fix at the format spec block: 'Closes 024A R6 R6-NEW-MAJ-002 (completeness — regex .{20,} vs prose ≥20 non-whitespace)'. Propagate to any other site citing the regex verbatim (R-024-06 line 219 cites the regex spec by reference, not literal, so only the format spec block itself needs changing).

findings.title: §5.6 first Threshold A criterion (plan-doc line 185) reads '≥3 of the 5 cohort adopters have policy-check/scp/policy-check required-check live + invocation log entries committed' — conflating the ≥3 counting criterion with the log-entry documentation requirement in a way inconsistent with §8's formulation, which separates them into distinct bullets
findings.evidence: Plan-doc §5.6 (line 185): '≥3 of the 5 cohort adopters have `policy-check / scp/policy-check` required-check live + invocation log entries committed.' This formulation makes 'invocation log entries committed' a necessary condition for an adopter to count toward the ≥3 Threshold A criterion. Plan-doc §8 (line 238) formulates the same counting criterion as: '≥3 of {PIM, recommender, mapp-doc-agent, control-tower, shopify-app} have `policy-check / scp/policy-check` as a required status check on default branch.' In §8, the log-entry requirement is a SEPARATE criterion in the following bullet (line 239): 'Each adopter that reached cascade-status: onboarded or cascade-status: onboarded-operator-bump has a corresponding entry in docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md...' The formulations are inconsistent: §5.6 counts only adopters with BOTH check-live AND log-entry toward ≥3; §8 counts adopters with check-live toward ≥3 and treats log-entry as a separate completeness requirement. In practice they are operationally equivalent (every check-live adopter via onboarded/onboarded-operator-bump paths has a log entry), but the formal specification is inconsistent. A reviewer using §5.6 as the Threshold A criterion would reach a different conclusion about whether log-entry absence precludes an adopter from the ≥3 count than a reviewer using §8. The severity is MIN rather than MAJ because: (a) the inconsistency has no practical operational impact (the paths are coupled); (b) this is a pre-existing inconsistency that was present before R5 and not introduced by any R5 fix (the companion sweep fixed §5.6 third bullet and §8 second bullet, not the first bullets of each). Fix-round-6 should align §5.6 first bullet with §8's cleaner formulation.
findings.recommendation: Update plan-doc §5.6 first Threshold A criterion (line 185) to align with §8's formulation. Replace '≥3 of the 5 cohort adopters have `policy-check / scp/policy-check` required-check live + invocation log entries committed' with '≥3 of the 5 cohort adopters have `policy-check / scp/policy-check` as a required status check on their default branch (only adopters whose cascade slice closed with cascade-status: onboarded or onboarded-operator-bump count; blocked-on-adopter-conflict adopters do NOT count toward this criterion until a successor sub-slice onboards them)'. The log-entry requirement for these adopters is already specified in §5.6 third bullet ('branch-protection-log.md is current (one entry per adopter that closed with cascade-status: onboarded or cascade-status: onboarded-operator-bump; conflict-close slices have NO entry per invariant 2's negative assertion)'); removing it from the first bullet eliminates the conflation. Add a closes marker: 'Closes 024A R6 R6-NEW-MIN-001 (§5.6 vs §8 Threshold A first criterion inconsistency)'.

pattern_observation: The R5 safety fix (adding the regex format spec to close the 'meaningful content not machine-enforceable' MAJ) introduced two new MAJ of the same class. This is the sixth consecutive round in which a fix to the cascade-status CI enforcement spec at invariant 2 introduced a propagation or precision gap. The pattern: each round's fix closes the cited gap at the cited site but introduces a new gap at a related dimension — either propagation to a different site (R2–R5) or internal consistency within the new spec text (R6). The R6 MAJs are within invariant 2's format spec block itself (not a cross-site propagation gap), which suggests the fix-round approach has now gone from 'add missing clauses' to 'resolve precision ambiguities within the clause'. Fix-round-6 should: (1) treat the format spec block as a single atomic unit requiring internal consistency review before submission; (2) resolve the regex-scope ambiguity by making the blocked-on-adopter-conflict path's TF filing location as explicit as the onboarded-operator-bump path's (which says 'STATUS.md Tracked-forward items row'); (3) do a targeted re-verify of both the regex clause and its prose description in the same pass to catch any introduced inconsistency before R7.
